podcast.title: 1990s Multi-Platinum Album Success
podcast.body: Blue Rodeo, which started as an "old country band," saw all of its albums released in the 1990s achieve multi-platinum sales. "All their 90s albums went multi-platinum."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Collaboration with Malcolm Burn
podcast.body: Malcolm Burn has produced and engineered for "Blue Road View." "With Dan's help Malcolm has had gigs producing an engineering for Iggy Pop and Patty Smith and Bob Dylan and Blue Road View and Midnight Oil and junk house and John Mellon Camp in many many more."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Contribution to Al Purdy Tribute
podcast.body: Bruce Cobra and Greg Keelor from Blue Rodeo were among the artists who contributed to the soundtrack of the 2015 documentary on Al Purdy, which featured songs and poems inspired by the poet. "Bruce Cobra and Greg Kieler of Blue Rodeo, Sarah Harmer, Jason Collette of Broken Social Scene, even Margaret Atwood appeared on that album."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Greg Keelor's Wise Advice on Music Career Options
podcast.body: While playing a show in Regina, 5440's Neil Osborne had a conversation with Greg Keelor of Blue Rodeo in the dressing room. When Neil confessed he couldn't imagine doing anything else if he stopped being a musician, Keelor offered a poignant piece of advice, "nice to know your options are behind you," highlighting the commitment and lack of alternative paths for long-term musicians. "Keylor came over to check out our set... I said to him... I don't think I could do anything else like if I had to stop this Being a musician thing. I don't think I could do anything else and he goes nice to know your options are behind you."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Late 1980s Success
podcast.body: Blue Rodeo was among the new acts signed throughout the late 1980s who achieved hits and solid-selling albums. This success was incentivized by the serious prospect of radio airplay, coverage by MuchMusic, and funding assistance, reflecting a growing investment in Canadian talent by the recorded music industry. "Throughout the late 1980s, new acts were signed and had hits in solid-selling albums, Blue Rodeo, The Box, Pursuit of Happiness, Northern Pikes, National Velvet, Alana Miles, 5440, Cowboy Junkeys."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Recording at The Bath House
podcast.body: Blue Rodeo recorded at The Bath House, The Tragically Hip's residential studio located west of Kingston, Ontario. "Blue rodeo, Ronnie Hawkins, Sam Roberts, Big Rec, and dozens and dozens of others have worked there."

xref.title: Final Public Performance (2017)
xref.body: On February 2, 2017, Gord Downie made his last public singing appearance at Massey Hall in Toronto, joining Blue Rodeo and opening act The Sadies on stage to perform "Lost Together." "And that would be the last time Gord ever sang in public."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Band Formation and Early Members
xref.body: Formed in Toronto in the late 1980s, Crash Vegas was co-founded by Michelle McAdory, daughter of Toronto TV news personality Bob McAdory, and Greg Keelor, who later joined Blue Rodeo. They started the band while they were dating. "One of the co-founders was Michelle McAdory, daughter of Bob, who was a fixture on Toronto TV news. She put the band together with Greg Keeler, and he asked that is the Greg Keeler who is now in Blue Rodeo. They were dating and thought that, well, you know, let's form a band."

xref.title: Early Lineup and Collaborations
xref.body: Michelle McAdory and Greg Keelor were joined by Jostelyn Lanois, sister of producer Daniel Lanois, on bass, and Ambrose Pottie on drums. The band frequently opened shows for Blue Rodeo. "Michelle and Greg were joined on base by Jostelyn Lamwaw, sister of Super producer Daniel Landwaw. And on drums was the spectacularly named Ambrose Putty. Crash Vegas opened a lot of shows for Blue Rodeo back then."

xref.title: Extensive Touring
xref.body: After the release of their debut album in 2001, Staggered Crossing embarked on tours with notable acts such as Nickelback, The Guess Who, Midnight Oil, Spirit of the West, Blue Rodeo, and Big Sugar, among others. "From there they toured with Nickelback, the Guess Who, Midnight Oil, Spirited the West, Blurodio, Big Sugar and others."

xref.title: Musician Friends' Benefit Concerts
xref.body: John Mann's musician friends, including members of the Barenaked Ladies, Blue Rodeo, and Sarah McLachlan, regularly organized benefit concerts to help fund his medical treatments. These events often featured collective performances of Spirit of the West classics. "And whenever one of these benefits was held, everybody joins in on this Spirit of the West class."

xref.title: Shift to Acting and Limited New Music
xref.body: Over the past two decades, Mary Margaret O'Hara has increasingly focused on acting roles in theater, film, and musicals. She has also continued to contribute to songs by other artists, such as Bob Wiseman of Blue Rodeo, with only one new song released under her own name in 2014. "In fact, Mary Margaret O'Hara has focused on acting over the last couple of decades, theater, film, musicals and so on, as well as contributing to songs of other artists such as Bob Weissman of Blue Rodeo. There was one new song in 2014, but that's been it."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: The Bathhouse Recording Studio
xref.body: The Tragically Hip owns and operates its own recording studio, known as The Bathhouse, located outside of Kingston. This studio has served as a recording location for numerous other artists, including Blue Rodeo, Big Rec, Sarah Harmer, Blackie and the Rodeo Kings, Hayden, The Sadies, Kathleen Edwards, The Trews, and The Mahones. "The hip has their own recording studio outside of Kingston called the Bathhouse. Blue Rodeo, Big Rec, Sarah Harmer, Blacky and the Rodeo Kings, Hayden, the Sadies, Kathleen Edwards, the Trues, the Mahones and dozens of others have used the place."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
